Easy.Description: Create a new curl object. Never lose this object until you are completely done with it. Never do 'Curl.Easy():Setopt' because this will cause the object to be lost by lua gc.
Easy.Example:
LuaCurl Curl.Easy()
curlObject = Curl.Easy()
curlObject:Setopt(eCurlOption.CURLOPT_URL, "https://www.google.com/"):Perform()
--Peform is an async task so keep the curlObject somewhere where it does not get freed from lua gc.

GetFinished.Description: Get whether or not the Perform call has finished.

GetResponse.Description: Get the response. The response string is only valid when no custom Write Function was used.

Perform.Description: Perform the curl operation after set up. Perform is called asynchronously. Call GetFinished() to check the current state.

Setopt.Description: Set specific curl options during initialize.
Setopt.Example:
LuaCurl object:Setopt(eCurlOption option, string str)
LuaCurl object:Setopt(eCurlOption option, int value)

Alloc.Description: Allocates a guarded block of size bytes and returns a pointer to its start. The block is zero-initialised, tracked for the lifetime of the script, surrounded by guard bytes to catch overflows, and freed automatically if the script forgets to. Read/Write/MemSet/String access on it is bounds-checked.

AllocInt.Description: Allocates a 4 byte guarded buffer where an integer can be stored.

Check.Description: Verifies the guard bytes of the allocation containing ptr. Returns true when intact; logs an error if an over/underflow is detected.

CheckGuards.Description: Verifies the guard bytes of every live allocation and returns the number of corrupted ones (0 means all good).

Free.Description: Deallocates a block of memory, making it available again for further allocations. Detects and reports double frees and invalid frees.

GetBaseAddress.Description: Returns the base address of the given module.

LuaCallCFunction.Description: Calls a function with user-defined arguments.

LuaCallCFunctionWithReturnValue.Description: Calls a function with user-defined arguments and returns a pointer to the return value. You must free the return value yourself using Memory.Free.

MemSet.Description: Sets the first num bytes of the block of memory pointed by ptr to the specified value (interpreted as an unsigned char).

add_page.Signature: features.add_page(label: string, ids: string[]) -> integer | nil, error: string?
add_page.Description: Game callback. Register a script-owned native feature page in BOTH ClickUI and ListUI Lua Content. Uses the actual command widgets and active native theme. Up to 64 pages per script, 256 exact IDs per page. Unload removes the owning script's pages.
add_page.Example:
local page = assert(features.add_page('My Self Tools', {'godmode'}))
-- Visible in ClickUI and ListUI Lua Content.
-- features.remove_page(page) removes it early.

call.Signature: features.call(id: string) -> boolean | nil, error: string?
call.Description: Game callback only. Executes an action through the main menu's Command.Call access checks. Value commands use features.set. IDs come from features.list, independently for each game.
call.Example:
script.run_in_fiber(function()
 for _, feature in ipairs(assert(features.list())) do
  if feature.type == 'action' then log.info(feature.id) end
 end
end)

get.Signature: features.get(id: string) -> Feature | nil, error: string?
get.Description: Game callback only. Fresh snapshot of the same command used by the main GUI and hotkeys. No raw pointers or private copied setting.
get.Example:
script.run_in_fiber(function()
 local feature, err = features.get('godmode')
 if feature then log.info(tostring(feature.value)) else log.info(err) end
end)

list.Signature: features.list(filter: string = '') -> Feature[] | nil, error: string?
list.Description: Game callback only. Sorted snapshots of registered host commands, with exact IDs, type, value, label, description, account availability, numeric bounds and list options. Case-sensitive substring filter matches ID or label. Runtime permission controls are excluded.
list.Example:
script.run_in_fiber(function()
 for _, feature in ipairs(assert(features.list('godmode'))) do
  log.info(feature.id .. ': ' .. tostring(feature.value))
 end
end)

remove_page.Signature: features.remove_page(pageId: integer) -> boolean | nil, error: string?
remove_page.Description: Game callback. Remove only a page owned by this Lua state. Returns false if missing or owned by another state. Retained native-page snapshots become inactive on removal or unload.

set.Signature: features.set(id: string, value: boolean|number|string|table) -> Feature | nil, error: string?
set.Description: Game callback only. Calls the actual typed setter, preserving callbacks and persistence. Validates type, finite numbers, integer bounds and real list option values; color/vector tables use x,y,z,w fields (colors 0..1). Preserves account restrictions. Returns the resulting snapshot, or nil and an error.
set.Example:
script.run_in_fiber(function()
 local state, err = features.set('godmode', true)
 if not state then log.info(err) end
end)

set_decal.Signature: panel.set_decal(key: string, texture_id: int, edge: string = "top", opts: table = nil) -> boolean
set_decal.Description: Pin an image to an edge of the menu window, free to overhang outside it - the "character peeking over the top of the menu" look. Re-using a key updates it in place. opts: width, height (0 = the texture's own size; setting only one derives the other from the aspect ratio so it is never stretched), along (0-1 down the edge, 0.5 centres), offset (extra pixels along the edge), overhang (pixels OUTSIDE the edge - match it to the height to sit fully outside), tint (packed ImU32), behind (draw under the window so it peeks out from behind instead of covering the chrome), visible, host ("both" | "clickui" | "listui"). Capped at 32 decals

 local snapshot = ui_theme.get()
 ui_theme.apply({clickui = snapshot.clickui})
end)

 -- Restore later with ui_theme.apply(savedTheme).
end)
